title: Tall cliff face, level top
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production artwork for Widow's Bay.
The same tall sea cliff as cliff-face-tall (pale layered rock with green ivy, jutting ledges at many heights, surf only at the very foot, no repeated section), with two changes: the grassy top is LEVEL and runs straight across the full width of the cliff within the top 3% of the image (the delivered one slopes down to the right, so the house on top floats), and the rock face keeps its full width all the way up instead of narrowing toward the top. The dark vertical crack runs from 20% to 80% of the height at about two-thirds of the width. Flat painted toy-theatre cut-out seen square-on, gouache on card with a faint pale cut edge; early-1900s stencil-tinted colour: sepia-grey line and tone with translucent washes of plum #2a1424, rose pink #f3c6dc, magenta #e0127a, moon gold #d9b34a, coral red #c8321e and grotto teal #5f8c88 laid slightly out of register; no cast shadow; no lettering; isolated on a transparent background (or flat pure magenta #FF00FF if transparency is unavailable).
Final image aspect ratio 1400:3600. Reference is the exact cliff edit target: keep pale layered rock, ivy, ledges, surf and gouache texture. Change its outer silhouette into a tall rectangle, with parallel near-vertical sides and the SAME WIDTH from bottom to top. Its grassy top is a single perfectly straight HORIZONTAL edge, perpendicular to sides, at y=2% of image height. No top hill, no slope, no narrowing/pyramid. Dark crack at x=66%, extending y=20% through80%. Leave only narrow transparent padding. Whole cliff, including level top and surf foot, visible. Actual transparent background.
